headline: Meta plans up to $95 billion in stock sales for AI buildout
body: Meta plans to sell up to $95 billion in shares to raise money for its AI infrastructure, according to The Information. A Meta announcement puts about $22.5 billion of that in Class A common stock, with $12.5 billion from depositary shares and the remaining $60 billion from open-market sales once new Class C shares start trading.
note: The Class C shares carry no voting rights, which lets Meta raise money without diluting Zuckerberg's control.

evidence.text: Meta plans to sell new stock to raise money for its AI infrastructure buildout.
According to The Information, the company plans to sell up to $95 billion in shares .
About $22.5 billion will come from selling Class A common stock, according to a Meta announcement .
Another $12.5 billion will come from depositary shares, each representing one-twentieth of a new preferred share.
The remaining $60 billion will come from ongoing sales on the open market once new Class C shares start trading, likely no earlier than the first quarter of 2027.
The Class C shares, which Meta announced last week, carry no voting rights.
That lets Meta raise money without diluting Zuckerberg's control.
